summary: Petition under Section 79 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 11 and 12 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Deviation Settlement Mechanism and Related Matters) Regulations, 2024 and Regulation 65 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 seeking appropriate directions for holding and declaring that the 160 MW Sui Generis Blended Wind Power Project (based on 81% wind component and 19% solar component) of the Petitioner be considered and treated as a generating station based on wind resource for the purpose of the CERC DSM Regulations, 2024 and more specifically under Regulation 8(4) of the CERC DSM Regulations, 2024. 6. The Petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 79 of the Electricity Act read with Regulations 11 and 12 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Deviation Settlement Mechanism and Related Matters) Regulations, 2024 (DSM Regulations,2024) and Regulation 65 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 (COB Regulations) seeking a declaration that its 160 MW Blended Wind Power Project be classified as a “generating station based on wind resource” for the purposes of the CERC DSM Regulations, 2024. - _(b) Hold and declare that in view of the peculiar facts and circumstances, the Petitioner’s Blended Wind Power Project should be treated as Wind Power Project for the purpose of the 2024 DSM Regulations as amended from time to time;_ - _(d) pass any other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case and interest of justice._ ## ** Submission by the Petitioner, Vena Energy Vidyuth Private Limited (VEVPL) ** - (e)On 07.09.2020 and 26.09.2020, the Petitioner applied for Stage-I and Stage-II connectivity to ISTS, respectively, for its Blended Wind Power Project. In this context, despite the project of the Petitioner being a Blended Wind Power Project, the Petitioner - (l) However, under the DSM Regulations, 2024, by erroneously categorising the Petitioner’s Blended Wind Power Project as a Hybrid Project and imposing deviation charges applicable to solar projects under Regulation 8(4), the Petitioner suffered a revenue loss of about 5.3%. 9. During the course of the hearing, the counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition was filed to seek appropriate directions to declare that the 160 MW Sui Generis Blended Wind Power Project of the Petitioner be considered and treated as a generating station based on wind resource for the purpose of Regulation 8(4) under DSM Regulations, 2024. After hearing the Petitioner’s counsel, the Commission admitted the Petition and directed the Respondents to file their reply and the Petitioner to file the rejoinder, if any. - (d)The contents of the Petition referring to the MNRE’s 2020 Blended Wind Guidelines, SECI bidding documents, and tariff adoption orders are matters between the Petitioner and the concerned procuring agencies. The bidding guidelines, schemes, and contractual arrangements cannot override or modify statutory regulations framed by the Commission under Section 178 of the Electricity Act, 2003, and the Petitioner's reliance on MNRE guidelines to seek re-classification under DSM Regulations is legally misconceived and unsustainable. ## ** Rejoinder by the Petitioner, Vena Energy, dated 18.02.2026, on the Reply submitted by the Respondent No. 1, SRPC ** - (d) SRPC itself acknowledged in the Reply that the PPA dated 03.05.2021 recognises and refers to the Petitioner as a Wind Power Developer. The said contractual recognition was not incidental; it flows directly from the policy framework of the 2020 Blended Wind Guidelines, which mandates a predominant wind component and permits limited solar blending only as an ancillary measure. ## ** Rejoinder by the Petitioner, Vena Energy, dated 18.02.2026, on the Reply submitted by ** - (a) In the present case, the Petitioner’s Blended Wind Power Project, having a predominantly wind-based character, is materially and fundamentally distinct from a hybrid project. It is a settled principle that unequal cannot be treated equally. - (b) The Petitioner’s sole and limited grievance pertains to classification, namely that a project conceived, bid and commissioned under the MNRE’s Blended Wind Scheme and the 2020 Blended Wind Guidelines, which permit limited solar blending up to 20%, has been categorised as a “generating station based on solar or a hybrid of wind-solar resources” under the DSM Regulations, 2024, despite being a predominantly wind-based Project. The Petitioner sought only correct classification, so that the deviation tolerance bands and settlement principles are applied equitably with the governing statutory and policy framework. 14. During the course of the hearing, on the request of the Petitioner, the Commission permitted the Petitioner to file its written submissions within a week. Subject to the above, the matter was reserved for order ## ** Written Submission by the Petitioner, Vena Energy, on 03.04.2026 in compliance with the ROP of the hearing dated 25.03.2026. ** 15. The Petitioner reiterated the contentions made in the petition as well as in the rejoinder and further mainly made the following submissions: 16. The Commission has heard the learned counsel for the Petitioner and the Respondents and considered their submissions, and has carefully perused the records. - _(i) Volume limits of a WS Seller for the period from_ **_the date of commencement of these regulations_** _to 31.03.2026 shall be as under:_ 24. The Commission further observes that accepting the contention of the Petitioner would require determination of a new threshold for distinguishing a predominantly wind-based blended project from a hybrid project under Regulation 8(4) of the DSM Regulations, 2024, which would be akin to an amendment of the Regulations.
